proposals.before: Li Xian, styled Xianhe, came from Chengji in Longxi.
proposals.after: Li Xian, styled Xianhe; his ancestors were men of Chengji in Longxi.
proposals.reason: Chinese 其先 marks ancestral origin, not that Li Xian himself was from Chengji.

proposals.before: At the end of Western Wei's Datong era, because the Xian brothers had won great distinction, their forebears were posthumously honored as Governors of Jing, Yuan, and Dongqin provinces and as Minister of Works.
proposals.after: At the end of Western Wei's Datong era, because the Xian brothers had won great distinction, their father was posthumously honored as Governor of Jing, Yuan, and Dongqin provinces and as Minister of Works.
proposals.reason: Following 父文保早卒, the silent subject of 追贈 is the father, not plural forebears.

proposals.before: At the end of Western Wei Datong, because the Xian brothers had distinguished merit, posthumously enfeoffed as Governor of Jing, Yuan, and Dongqin provinces and Minister of Works.
proposals.after: At the end of Western Wei Datong, because the Xian brothers had distinguished merit, their father was posthumously granted Governor of Jing, Yuan, and Dongqin provinces and Minister of Works.
proposals.reason: 追贈 is a posthumous office grant, not an enfeoffment, and the recipient is the father named in s0005.

proposals.before: During Western Wei's Yong'an era, Moqi Chounu rebelled and seized Qi, Jing, and neighboring provinces; Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei sent Erzhu Tianguang to crush him.
proposals.after: During Northern Wei's Yong'an era, Moqi Chounu rebelled and seized Qi, Jing, and neighboring provinces; Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei sent Erzhu Tianguang to crush him.
proposals.reason: 永安 under Emperor Xiaozhuang is a Northern Wei reign, not Western Wei.

proposals.before: As the main force neared Qin Province, Yue abandoned the city and fled. Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sent his grandnephew Dao in pursuit with Li Xian as vanguard.
proposals.after: As the main force neared Qin Province, Yue abandoned the city and fled. Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sent his nephew Dao in pursuit with Li Xian as vanguard.
proposals.reason: 兄子 is a brother's son (nephew), not a grandnephew.

proposals.before: When the grand army was about to reach Qin Province, Yue abandoned the city and fled; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai ordered his nephew's son Dao to lead troops in pursuit, with Xian as vanguard.
proposals.after: When the grand army was about to reach Qin Province, Yue abandoned the city and fled; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai ordered his brother's son Dao to lead troops in pursuit, with Xian as vanguard.
proposals.reason: 兄子 means brother's son, not nephew's son.

proposals.before: Ning did not follow and repeatedly fought and frequently lost northward.
proposals.after: Ning did not follow and repeatedly fought and frequently suffered defeat.
proposals.reason: 頻北 means repeated defeat (北 as to be defeated), not geographic northward loss.

proposals.before: He again comforted and reassured Zhangye and the other five commanderies and returned.
proposals.after: He then comforted and reassured Zhangye and the other commanderies among the five, and returned.
proposals.reason: 等五郡 means five commanderies including Zhangye, not five additional commanderies besides Zhangye.

proposals.before: While Emperor Gaozu and Prince of Qi Yuwen Hu were still infants, taboo made it inauspicious for them to remain in the palace.
proposals.after: While Emperor Gaozu and Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian were still infants, taboo made it inauspicious for them to remain in the palace.
proposals.reason: Chinese 齊王憲 names the Prince of Qi as Xian (憲), not Yuwen Hu (護).

proposals.before: When Emperor Gaozu and Prince of Qi Yuwen Hu were still in swaddling clothes, to avoid taboo it was inauspicious for them to live in the palace.
proposals.after: When Emperor Gaozu and Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian were still in swaddling clothes, to avoid taboo it was inauspicious for them to live in the palace.
proposals.reason: Chinese 齊王憲 is Yuwen Xian, Prince of Qi; the English wrongly substitutes Yuwen Hu.

proposals.before: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai had them lodged at Yu Xian's household; only after six years did they return to the palace.
proposals.after: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai had them lodged at Xian's household; only after six years did they return to the palace.
proposals.reason: 賢 is Li Xian throughout the chapter; rendering the household as Yu Xian invents a different surname.

proposals.before: Rebel factions seized the moment and spread their poison.
proposals.after: The Hun faction seized the moment and spread their poison.
proposals.reason: 匈黨 names a Xiongnu/Hun faction; generic rebels omits that label.

proposals.before: Later, for his service under Houmochen Chong, he was transferred to Administrator of Gaoping.
proposals.after: Later, for merit in answering Houmochen Chong, he was transferred to Administrator of Gaoping.
proposals.reason: 應侯莫陳崇功 is meritorious response to Houmochen Chong, not merely service under him.

proposals.before: At Shayuan Li Yuan's merit ranked first; he was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Three Departments, and raised to Duke of Yangping with a fief of three thousand households.
proposals.after: At Shayuan, Li Yuan's merit ranked first; he was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Three Departments, and raised to Duke of Yangping with a fief of three thousand households.
proposals.reason: Missing comma fuses the battlefield name Shayuan with the personal name Li Yuan.

proposals.before: He was summoned as attendant-in-ordinary, grand general of rapid cavalry, and opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol.
proposals.after: He was summoned as Palace Attendant, Grand General of Rapid Cavalry, and Opening Office with Equal-to-Three-Ministers honors.
proposals.reason: The calque of 開府儀同三司 is unintelligible as an office title.

proposals.before: At that time Gao Huan had encamped at Hene.
proposals.after: At that time Gao Huan had encamped at Heyang.
proposals.reason: 河陽 is Heyang, not Hene (河內).

proposals.before: At that time Qi Divine Warrior Gao Huan had encamped his troops at Hene.
proposals.after: At that time Qi Divine Warrior Gao Huan had encamped his troops at Heyang.
proposals.reason: 河陽 is Heyang, not Hene.

proposals.before: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was pleased and said: "What Li Wan Sui has said is rather to my liking."
proposals.after: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was pleased and said: "What Li Wansui has said is rather to my liking."
proposals.reason: 李萬歲 is the courtesy name Wansui, not three English words Wan Sui.

proposals.before: The Grand Progenitor was pleased and said: "What Li Wan Sui has said is rather to one's liking."
proposals.after: The Grand Progenitor was pleased and said: "What Li Wansui has said is rather to one's liking."
proposals.reason: 李萬歲 should be transcribed as Wansui.

proposals.before: Before long, he was removed and made left vice director of the secretariat.
proposals.after: Before long, he was appointed left vice director of the secretariat.
proposals.reason: 除 here means to appoint, not to remove.

proposals.before: Duke Jue of Lueyang should be heir apparent—what doubt has Your Grace?
proposals.after: The Duke of Lüeyang should be heir apparent—what doubt has Your Grace?
proposals.reason: 畧陽公 is the ducal title only; the given name Jue is not in this sentence.

proposals.before: Duke Jue of Lueyang should be heir apparent—what doubt has Your Grace?
proposals.after: The Duke of Lüeyang should be heir apparent—what doubt has Your Grace?
proposals.reason: 畧陽公 does not include the personal name Jue in the source.

proposals.before: Later, because of his father's merit, he was enfeoffed Duke of Jiang'an county with a fief of one thousand households.
proposals.after: Later, because of his father's merit, he was enfeoffed Duke of Jian'an county with a fief of one thousand households.
proposals.reason: 建安 is Jian'an, not Jiang'an; the English invents a different place-name.

proposals.before: Because his patron had status and because his paternal uncle Li Mu pleaded for him, he was spared.
proposals.after: Because his consort was of high rank and because his paternal uncle Li Mu pleaded for him, he was spared.
proposals.reason: 主貴 refers to his princess-consort's rank, not a generic patron.

proposals.before: The historiographer writes: Li Xianhe and his brothers lived through civil collapse amid constant warfare; bold in design and fierce in loyalty, they repeatedly broke strong enemies and often faced mortal danger—yet their achievements went unrecorded at court, and their posts never rose above the prefectural level.
proposals.after: The historiographer writes: Li Xian and his brothers lived through civil collapse amid constant warfare; bold in design and fierce in loyalty, they repeatedly broke strong enemies and often faced mortal danger—yet their achievements went unrecorded at court, and their posts never rose above the prefectural level.
proposals.reason: 李賢和兄弟 is Li Xian plus his brothers, not a single name Li Xianhe; 和 is the conjunction 'and'.

proposals.before: The historiographer says: Li Xianhe and his brothers, amid disorder and separation, lived among campaigns and horses; their plans were far-ranging, their loyalty and courage ardent; they repeatedly crushed formidable foes and often passed through peril—yet their merit was not recorded in the princely house, and their offices did not exceed prefecture and commandery.
proposals.after: The historiographer says: Li Xian and his brothers, amid disorder and separation, lived among campaigns and horses; their plans were far-ranging, their loyalty and courage ardent; they repeatedly crushed formidable foes and often passed through peril—yet their merit was not recorded in the princely house, and their offices did not exceed prefecture and commandery.
proposals.reason: The same 李賢和兄弟 split is misread as the fused personal name Li Xianhe in the literal rendering.

decisions.reason: 其先 marks ancestral origin; the original makes Li Xian himself a native of Chengji, against the following settlement at Gaoping.

decisions.reason: 追贈 is a posthumous office grant to the father of s0005, not an enfeoffment; the proposal still reads awkwardly without naming the offices granted.

Without the comma, Shayuan can be read as fused with Li Yuan; 沙苑之役 is the battle-place, then 遠.
侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司 are standard offices; the calque ‘opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol’ is unintelligible.
